hypothesis: If bats occur on almost every oceanic island and often as endemics, then most islands in a pre-specified list of oceanic islands and archipelagos have at least one bat record in GBIF, and a substantial fraction of the remote ones have a bat species confined to them.
pass_criterion: Of the 30 pre-listed oceanic islands or archipelagos (volcanic or coral, never continentally connected), at least 80% (24 or more) have at least one GBIF Chiroptera occurrence with coordinates falling on the island or archipelago, excluding fossil or subfossil records. Also, among the pre-listed islands that are at least 1000 km from the nearest continent, at least 40% have at least one bat species whose GBIF records worldwide all fall within that island or archipelago, which I count as endemic.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% (under 18 of 30) of the listed islands have any GBIF bat occurrence, or fewer than 20% of the islands at least 1000 km from a continent have an endemic bat species. Between these bounds the result is inconclusive and the claim is not confirmed. The list is fixed before querying: Azores, Madeira, Canaries, Cape Verde, Bermuda, Hawaii, Galápagos, Juan Fernández, Falklands, Tristan da Cunha, St Helena, Ascension, Mauritius, Réunion, Rodrigues, Comoros, Seychelles, Kerguelen, Christmas Island (Indian Ocean), Fiji, Samoa, Tonga, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, Society Islands, Marquesas, Cook Islands, Palau and Marianas, and Norfolk and Lord Howe.
interpretation: Darwin's 'ærial mammals' means bats (Chiroptera). 'Oceanic islands' means islands never joined to a continent, taken as the fixed list above. 'Almost every island' is operationalised as at least 80% of that list having a bat record. 'Often endemic' is operationalised as at least 40% of the remote islands (1000 km or more from a continent) having a bat species restricted to that island or archipelago. Modern reinterpretation: endemism is judged from the global spatial footprint of GBIF occurrences, not from 1859 taxonomy. Records are filtered to preserved specimens and human observations with coordinates and no geospatial issues. Island membership is determined by the coordinates or the Darwin Core island, islandGroup and countryCode fields. Known absences, such as bats on Ascension, St Helena or Kerguelen, are counted as failures and not excluded. The test is limited by recording effort and by GBIF taxonomy.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (Chiroptera, searchable and downloadable via GBIF.org)
dataset.why_it_fits: GBIF serves worldwide specimen and observation records through a free API (https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search) and downloads. Filtering on order Chiroptera, country, island and islandGroup, coordinates, basisOfRecord and species key gives per-island presence of bats. Comparing each species' global footprint against the island gives endemism. The fields used are speciesKey, scientificName, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, countryCode, island, islandGroup, basisOfRecord and hasGeospatialIssues. A GBIF download would receive its own DOI when it is made. I have not checked the landing page or the order's taxon key in this session.
